figures.caption: (A) The minimal hemolytic activity in mice (MHC), GMMIC, and TI values of the engineered peptides. aThe average hydrophobicity (H) values were determined by dividing the sum of all residue hydrophobicity indices by the number of residues. These calculations were performed using an online tool available at http://heliquest.ipmc.cnrs.fr/cgi-bin/ComputParams.py. bMHC refers to the minimum concentration at which 10 % hemolysis of mouse red blood cells occurred. The data presented in this study were obtained from three independent experiments. In cases where no measurable hemolytic activity was observed at 128 μM, a value of 256 μM was utilized for calculating the TI. cGMMIC is the geometric mean of MIC values against yeas. The calculation of dTI involves dividing MHC by GMMIC. Higher values suggest enhanced cell selectivity. (B) Relationship between the GMMIC and H values of the engineered peptides. (C) The FIC indexes for the GW4 in combination with antifungal drugs against C. albicans cgmcc 2.2086. FIC index < 0.5 as synergy, 0.5 < FICI < 1.0 as additive, 1.0 < FICI < 4.0 as indifferent, and FICI > 4.0 as antagonism. aThe MIC values of Fluconazole, Ketoconazole, and Amphotericin B were 8 μM, 8 μM, and 0.25 μM, respectively, against C. albicans cgmcc 2.2086. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)
